phase3_findings.description: scripts/telemetry-master-off.py's docstring line 'Single source of PRFlow's telemetry master-switch predicate (issue #2035).' is false against HEAD: the same diff ships three independent implementations of the predicate (this script, the inline python3 -c in scripts/config-get.sh's telemetry_master_disables_for, and the inline python3 -c in lib/efficiency-trace.sh's do_persist), and only scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh execs the .py. The two inline copies carry comments explaining why they deliberately do NOT call it (the issue-#458 Stop-hook closure drift-guard), so the diff contradicts itself. Nothing mechanically couples the three, so a later semantics fix applied to one leaves the other two stale and the suite stays green. The same misdescription recurs in .prflow/config.schema.json ('Read at RUNTIME through scripts/config-get.sh (and scripts/telemetry-master-off.py)') and docs/internal/DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md line 1144, both of which read as though config-get.sh delegates to the script. Remedy: restate the docstring as the exec-able form of the predicate, name the two inline mirrors as coupled sites in all three places, and optionally pin the three arms against one fixture matrix.

phase3_findings.description: The shipped claim that an explicitly-set sub-key always wins over the master 'in both directions' is false for the efficiency-trace mechanism. docs/external/docs/configuration/observability-and-privacy.md says 'An explicit key always wins... it overrides the master, in both directions - so you can turn the master off but keep one mechanism on', and .prflow/config.schema.json says 'A sub-key a consumer has set explicitly ALWAYS wins over this master, in both directions'. Verified empirically on HEAD: with telemetry.enabled=false and an explicit prflow_review_and_fix.efficiency_telemetry_enabled=true, lib/efficiency-trace.sh --persist still emits its skip breadcrumb, never creates refs/heads/prflow-telemetry, and returns 0 - because do_persist's new guard reads telemetry.enabled directly while --persist is itself already gated by efficiency_telemetry_enabled. A second, narrower counterexample: an enrolled sub-key explicitly set to JSON null or the empty string falls to emit_default_or_fail and therefore inherits the master's false rather than the caller default. Remedy: either consult the sub-key in the two push-path guards, or qualify both sentences to the resolver path and the absent/unset-key case.
phase3_findings.cap_analysis: Behavior-inert prose cap NOT applied. Limb two fails outright: this is a published external documentation page (and the config schema description) read by consumers outside this repository. Not inert -> Phase 4.2 self-contradicting-diff carve-out.

phase3_findings.description: The changeset ('turn off PRFlow's optional telemetry in one switch') and the external docs ('every optional telemetry mechanism turns off in one place') assert a universal the enrolled set does not deliver: prflow.execution_transcript_artifact_enabled is an optional telemetry mechanism that is deliberately not enrolled, so a consumer who set it to true keeps the scrubbed transcript artifact uploading under a false master. The exclusion is defensible (it defaults to false), but the shipped sentences state 'every', and the changeset text lands in the published CHANGELOG. Remedy: name the enrolled set, or say 'every default-on optional telemetry mechanism'.
phase3_findings.cap_analysis: Behavior-inert prose cap NOT applied. Limb two fails: the changeset text becomes the published CHANGELOG entry and the docs page is consumer-facing. Not inert -> Phase 4.2 self-contradicting-diff carve-out.

phase3_findings.description: scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh's new gate reads the config at the literal path "$ROOT/.prflow/config.json", bypassing both the state-directory read-through (lib/resolve-state-dir.sh / prflow_state_dir, which scripts/config-get.sh uses) and DEVFLOW_CONFIG_FILE (which lib/config-source.sh honours and which the sibling lib/efficiency-trace.sh guard therefore does honour via $_DEVFLOW_CONFIG). A consumer mid-migration whose config still lives at .devflow/config.json and who set telemetry.enabled=false has the predicate read a nonexistent file, exit 1, and the collector stages and pushes telemetry anyway - the exact deployment shape the transitional read-through exists for. The two push-path guards in this one PR therefore disagree about which file the master lives in. Fail-safe in direction, but it contradicts the 'one switch / every mechanism' claim for that population and no test covers it.

phase3_findings.description: Both new gates fail open silently on every non-config reason. scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh's guard is a three-term && chain (helper present, python3 present, predicate exits 0); a missing helper, an absent or broken python3, or an unreadable config falls through to collect-and-upload with no output at all, while every other failure arm in that same file breadcrumbs. lib/efficiency-trace.sh's do_persist guard has the same shape and the same missing arm. The generic fail-safe-to-ON rationale is imported from the per-key observability gates, but this one is the consumer's privacy switch: a repository that set telemetry.enabled=false and lost python3 from a self-hosted runner's PATH keeps pushing to a long-lived branch and is never told the switch was not evaluated. Remedy: split the chain so an unevaluable predicate emits its own ::warning:: naming what could not be evaluated.

scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh's _CST_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" && pwd)" leaves the string unchanged when BASH_SOURCE[0] carries no slash (a bare-name PATH invocation); cd then fails, _CST_DIR is empty, the [ -f "$_CST_DIR/telemetry-master-off.py" ] test is false, and the gate silently no-ops into finding F5's fail-open. The comment directly above names that hazard as the reason for the dirname-free form without guarding it. The only in-tree call site passes a slash-bearing path, so this is latent rather than live. Remedy: case "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" in */*) ... ;; *) _CST_DIR=. ;; esac, or breadcrumb when the anchor cannot be resolved.

docs/external/docs/configuration/observability-and-privacy.md states telemetry-off 'saves only a small amount of run time (measured at roughly 1-3% of a run)'. Under the prefer-generated-evidence convention (issue #656) a figure a reader treats as current must be rendered live or registered as an exempt literal with a rationale; this is neither an enforcement constant, a dated past-time snapshot, nor a future target, so it rots invisibly in consumer-facing docs. The figure does trace to the issue's own text, so it is not fabricated. Remedy: drop the parenthetical (the sentence's point survives) or attribute it as a dated measurement.

Three added inline comment blocks exceed the prevention-only standard's three-physical-line cap: lib/efficiency-trace.sh do_persist (6 lines), scripts/config-get.sh telemetry_master_disables_for (3 + 4 lines), scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh (5 lines). Their substance is right - each names a wrong change it prevents (adding a source/exec edge that would break the issue-#458 drift-guard; using == False, which would let the JSON number 0 disable telemetry) - but the surrounding derivation and provenance belong in internal docs. The #458 rationale is additionally restated verbatim across two files, which the restatement rule prohibits. Remedy: keep the prohibition-and-consequence sentence in each, capped at three lines, and move the derivation to docs/internal/.
